headline: Sequence models and multiomic atlases sharpen noncoding variant effect prediction
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Prediction
summary: MPRA-supervised Borzoi fine-tuning, Enformer-based eQIF scoring and single-molecule chromatin models all target regulatory variant interpretation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring regulatory consequences of noncoding variants from sequence and functional genomic context. Sequence-to-function models are being adapted for variant scoring: Borzoi fine-tuned on synthetic MPRA variant-effect labels improves CAGI5 and eQTL correlations while preserving pre-trained tracks, and eQIF uses isolation forests to collapse Enformer outputs into one unsupervised score per common variant. Variant prioritization also draws on curated evidence: mV2G integrates 24 evidence types across 50 tissues with a CRISPR-informed model, Wreath predicts methylation-level variant effects from a 90+ tissue compendium, and XGBoost-SHAP on pancreatic progenitor snATAC-seq prioritizes HNF4A motif-disrupting SNPs. A second strand shifts targets to single-molecule chromatin: ChAI-Net predicts co-accessibility, Mola predicts per-molecule accessibility distributions, and FiberBrowser standardizes footprinting inference. CellReg3D (Hi-C plus DNA language model embeddings), MUSS (multi-scale single-cell) and CNN-CR (cell-type-specific motif interpretation) extend cell-type context.
